Watcom field-by-field struct copy (3 consecutive `dst.field = src.field;` lines). Replace with `dst = src;` or `memcpy(&dst, &src, sizeof(...));` in a .keep — but only once the run (together with any sibling runs for the same dst/src pair) covers every byte of the struct. Collapsing a run that leaves a gap WIDENS the copy and changes behaviour; see `partial_struct_copy` (§31) for that case.

Watcom dead self-copy guard: `if (&fStack_254 != &fStack_188)` wraps an unconditional struct copy. Both addresses are stack locals — always different — so the guard never skips. Drop the if-wrapper in a .keep.

Watcom shadow-pointer walk — `pCVar2` self-updates via the address of a constant index into itself plus a subfield path, where `N*sizeof(*pCVar2) + offsetof(subfield)` equals the real array stride. Replace `pCVar2->some_field[0]` (or the zero-index access) reads with direct indexing on the original pointer; drop the shadow init and self-update.
